name: Telephone exchange
simple: The phone company’s exchange connects your call to the internet company, like a giant switchboard. It keeps the line open for as long as you stay online.
technical: The local exchange switches the call: the copper loop ends here, and the call goes on as a 64 kbit/s digital timeslot through the phone network to the ISP’s modems.

peek.simple: The exchange doesn’t open anything: it just carries your call, sound and all, on to the internet company.
peek.technical: Circuit-switched: the call goes on as a 64 kbit/s timeslot. Nothing here reads a frame; the PPP frames ride inside the modems’ sound.
